<!--
Before submitting a PR, please read https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/dev/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md#pull-request-guidelines

1. Give the PR a descriptive title.

  Examples of good title:
    - fix(windows): fix race condition in event loop
    - docs: update example for `App::show`
    - feat: add `Window::set_fullscreen`

  Examples of bad title:
    - fix #7123
    - update docs
    - fix bugs

2. If there is a related issue, reference it in the PR text, e.g. closes #123.
3. If this change requires a new version, then add a change file in `.changes` directory with the appropriate bump, see https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/dev/.changes/README.md
4. Ensure that all your commits are signed https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/managing-commit-signature-verification/signing-commits
5. Ensure `cargo test` and `cargo clippy` passes.
6. Propose your changes as a draft PR if your work is still in progress.
-->
fix(#13287): allow the target directory to be inside frontendDir as long as it is not the Rust target directory inside frontendDir.

comments.body: This section doesn't make much sense. get_cargo_target_dir will return an absolute path and so will overwrite tauri_path. joining it to the tauri_path may not be correct for relative paths either i think.
web_asset_path is not canonicalized yet (the canonicalize call in line 169 does not carry over) so this check may be false for the same directories.
this check is incorrect, we check if they are the node_modules or src-tauri folders, neither are the cargo target path. In other words, we just need the is_dir check here like it was before.
sorry, forgot that in the first review. the outer `if target_path.starts_with(&web_asset_canonical) {` can be removed since strip_prefix already includes that check as well.
